findings.rule: Every order requires `model_tier` (decision 87), in lowercase letters and digits only, so that no name reads two ways.
findings.finding: The order passes the check although its name also reads as pass `prose` on tier `opus`, because `pass` may hold a hyphen followed by a tier word, so the opus filter `order/[0-9a-z-]+-opus-.*` picks an order whose `model_tier` is `sonnet`.

findings.rule: The check walks the name part by part against the order's fields and names the part that disagrees: role, pass, model_tier, subject or step.
findings.input: orders/review-spec-fidelity-opus-r2-pando58-4.yml with `role: reviewer`, `pass: spec-fidelity`, `model_tier: opus`, `subject: pandoscope/pandoscope#58` (the old `-r2` in the middle of a name)
findings.finding: The violation reads "the model_tier part must be 'opus', and the name reads 'opus-r2-pando58-4' there", so it names model_tier as the part that is off although the name's tier agrees with the order's `model_tier`.

findings.rule: An order whose name is off its pattern, or disagrees with its role, pass, tier or subject, fails the order check, and the message says which part.
findings.input: orders/implement-opus-pando57-1.yml with `id: implement-opus-pando57-1`, `role: probe`, `model_tier: opus`, `subject: pandoscope/pandoscope#57`, `tickets: []`
findings.finding: The order passes with "ok, but the role 'probe' has no name pattern" although its name is the implementer pattern and so disagrees with its role; the pull request body declares the rest of such a name unchecked.
